hero.name: LAUAI ALERFI
hero.title: SYSTEMS ENGINEER
hero.desc: VLSI / IC Design · FPGA / HDL · Embedded Systems · Control Systems · Software Dev · Guelph, Canada
overview: I'm a Systems Engineering graduate from the University of Guelph (B.Eng, April 2026), specializing in the intersection of hardware design and software development.

I work at every layer of the stack, from designing CMOS circuits at the transistor level in Cadence Virtuoso to implementing FPGA SoC systems in VHDL/Verilog to building enterprise apps in C# and ASP.NET.

Currently a Software/Systems Developer at ECNG Energy Group, building AI-powered pipelines with the Claude API and Python automation. I love engineering problems that live at the boundary of hardware and software, where the logic meets the physics. Originally from Damascus, Syria, now building things in Canada.

experience.title: Software / Systems Developer
experience.desc: AI invoice extraction service (Python, FastAPI, Claude API) feeding a C# billing app, 97% match across 265 utilities with a 22 invoice regression suite; daily IESO price alert pipeline with per client thresholds, in production since May 2026; Playwright portal automation across 110 customer accounts with zero errors; Selenium scraper fixes taking 208 monthly reports from 27 failures to zero; Microsoft Graph mailbox service filing utility reports into SQL Server.

projects.title: 8-bit CMOS Program Counter
bullets: Designed a fully functional 8-bit Program Counter at the transistor level using Cadence Virtuoso with the gpdk045 45nm CMOS process
Implemented three sub-modules from scratch: a CMOS transmission gate multiplexer, a mirror adder ripple carry full adder, and a master-slave D flip-flop register
Achieved a critical path delay of 906 ps, meeting the 1 GHz minimum frequency requirement with a theoretical maximum operating frequency of 1.10 GHz
Measured average power consumption of 58.08 µW through Spectre transient simulation
Characterized each module individually for worst-case propagation delay: 738 ps (full adder), 394 ps (register CLK-to-Q), and 143 ps (multiplexer)
Verified correct sequential increment and branch operation through full top-level transient simulation
Documented design decisions, timing analysis, and simulation results in a 17-page technical report

projects.title: 8×8 6T SRAM Macro, Sky130
projects.spec: 716 mV SNM · DRC/LVS-clean · AI-agent driven · 130nm
bullets: Designed a full-custom 6T SRAM macro (64-bit, 8×8) from scratch in SkyWater Sky130 130nm PDK, every transistor hand-placed in Magic, no standard cells

Built and verified the complete cell library bottom-up: 6T bit cell, 3-to-8 row decoder, precharge/equalize, write driver, and cross-coupled sense amplifier, all DRC-clean, LVS-matched, and SPICE-verified
Integrated decoder + 8×8 array + read/write data-path periphery into a single DRC-clean macro; characterized static noise margin via butterfly curves (716 mV hold / 311 mV read)

Used Claude AI agents as the execution layer, directing them to author Magic/ngspice scripts and run DRC checks, layout extractions, and SPICE simulations in parallel across background jobs, iterating far faster than a manual GUI flow while steering the architecture and verification calls
Drove the entire flow headlessly and reproducibly, layout, DRC, extraction, and simulation all scripted (Magic + ngspice), so every result is one command away from being regenerated
Whole-macro extraction caught a bug a clean DRC missed: the decoder-to-array word-line routing was design-rule-clean but electrically open, found it, fixed the routing, confirmed connectivity
Simulating the extracted layout surfaced a real cell write-ability margin between schematic and silicon, exactly the schematic-vs-extracted gap that full-custom verification exists to catch
alts: Full macro layout with row decoder

projects.title: AES-128 Hardware Coprocessor
projects.spec: NIST verified · APB-integrated · CBC/OFB modes
bullets: Designed and implemented a 128-bit AES encryption coprocessor in Verilog targeting an FPGA-based SoC platform
Developed a custom APB (Advanced Peripheral Bus) IP module and integrated it into the system using Platform Designer
Built a memory-mapped hardware/software interface enabling communication between the HPS processor and FPGA coprocessor
Implemented core AES transformations: SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, and AddRoundKey following NIST standards, plus full key expansion logic for AES-128
Developed a fully combinational (asynchronous) AES architecture, optimizing latency by eliminating clock dependency in the encryption core
Supported secure encryption modes (CBC/OFB) for improved data security beyond basic ECB mode
Verified functionality using official NIST test vectors; debugged and validated system integration across hardware (FPGA) and software (C driver on HPS)
alts: AES-128 CBC NIST PASS terminal output

projects.title: Custom Synchronous CPU
projects.spec: Full RTL datapath · FSM control · FPGA synthesized
bullets: Designed and implemented a custom synchronous CPU at the RTL level using VHDL, targeting FPGA implementation
Architected a multi-stage datapath including register file, ALU, control unit, and memory interface
Developed FSM-based control logic to manage instruction fetch, decode, execution, and write-back sequencing
Applied computer architecture principles to define instruction behavior, datapath/control separation, and signal timing
Performed functional simulation and waveform-level debugging in ModelSim to verify correctness and timing
Synthesized and implemented the design in Xilinx Vivado, analyzing timing closure, critical paths, and resource utilization

projects.title: FPGA Accelerator, Vivado HLS
projects.spec: Loop pipelining · Array partitioning · Dataflow architecture
bullets: Designed a hardware accelerator kernel in C/C++ and targeted FPGA implementation using Vivado HLS on a Xilinx Zynq SoC
Applied loop pipelining, loop unrolling, and dataflow architectures to improve throughput and reduce latency of compute-intensive kernels
Optimized memory access using array partitioning and memory reshaping to remove bandwidth bottlenecks
Analyzed HLS synthesis and implementation reports to evaluate clock frequency, latency, initiation interval (II), and DSP/LUT/BRAM utilization
Integrated the accelerator with ARM-side software on Zynq, validating correct HW/SW interaction against C/C++ reference models
Developed Python scripts to automate performance analysis, compare design variants, and verify functional equivalence

projects.title: ARINC 429 Transmitter & Receiver
projects.spec: Full protocol · FSM-based Rx · Nexys A7
bullets: Designed and implemented a complete ARINC 429 transmitter and receiver in VHDL, targeting the Nexys A7 FPGA
Implemented 32-bit ARINC word formatting including label fields, SDI, data, SSM decoding, and odd parity generation and checking
Developed an FSM-based receiver for bit timing, word detection, parity validation, and protocol error handling
Implemented a protocol-compliant transmitter with MSB-first bit ordering and timing behavior aligned with ARINC 429 specifications
Verified functional correctness and timing behavior through RTL simulation and waveform analysis in ModelSim
Optimized RTL design in Xilinx Vivado, reducing LUT and flip-flop utilization while maintaining strict protocol timing constraints

projects.title: Direct Polymer Extrusion 3D Printer
projects.spec: 30 to 50% cost reduction · STM32 SKR Mini E3 · Capstone
bullets: Designed and implemented a Direct Polymer Extrusion system by modifying a Creality 3D printer to print directly from raw polymer material, eliminating the need for filament
Replaced the stock control board with an STM32-based controller (SKR Mini E3) to support custom hardware integration
Configured and modified Marlin firmware to enable compatibility with a non-standard extrusion system
Integrated and configured a custom display interface to ensure seamless operation with the upgraded control board
Tuned key system parameters including extrusion rate, temperature profiles, and motion synchronization to achieve stable and consistent printing performance
Solved system-level challenges involving hardware, software integration, real-time control, and thermal management
Enabled multi-material printing and direct use of recycled plastics; achieved 30 to 50% cost reduction with up to 75% savings when using bulk polymer pellets

projects.title: Real-Time Hot Air Plant Control
projects.spec: FreeRTOS tasks · Closed-loop PID · Queue/Semaphore sync
bullets: Developed real-time embedded firmware in C for an ARM-based microcontroller using FreeRTOS, built and debugged with Keil and STM32CubeIDE
Architected a task-based RTOS system with dedicated tasks for temperature sensing, control computation, actuator output, and system monitoring
Interfaced temperature sensors via ADC, implemented signal conditioning, and validated sensor accuracy and response time
Implemented closed-loop control logic to regulate air temperature by dynamically adjusting heater power and fan operation under real-time constraints
Used FreeRTOS inter-task communication mechanisms (queues and semaphores) to ensure deterministic data flow between sensing, control, and actuation
Debugged timing, synchronization, and control behavior using oscilloscope-based measurements and runtime task analysis
alts: Real-time hot air plant control setup
FreeRTOS task timing and sensor output

projects.title: G.U.I.D.E., Wearable LiDAR System
projects.spec: 360° LiDAR oscillation · Haptic feedback · ~12 hr battery
bullets: Designed a wearable real-time obstacle detection system combining a 360° 2D LiDAR mounted on a motorized oscillation mechanism to achieve effective 3D spatial sensing for head- and body-level hazards
Developed control logic to process LiDAR distance, angle data, convert polar measurements into real-world coordinates, and classify actionable obstacles using calibrated reference thresholds
Implemented a stepper-motor, driven scanning architecture, synchronizing motor position, IMU orientation, and LiDAR sampling to maintain consistent spatial mapping during user motion
Designed a ground-level hazard detection subsystem using a cane-mounted rotary encoder and contact switch to detect traction loss and slippery surfaces in real time
Engineered directional haptic feedback logic, mapping obstacle proximity and direction to multiple vibration motors to deliver intuitive, low-latency tactile alerts

Performed system-level validation including torque calculations, battery life modeling (~12 hours), sensitivity analysis, and compliance with accessibility standards (Accessible Canada Act, EN 301 549)

projects.title: Embedded Digital Voltmeter System
projects.spec: STM32 · ADC/SPI/I2C · signal conditioning · oscilloscope validated
bullets: Developed embedded firmware in C for an ARM-based STM32 microcontroller to measure and display analog voltages
Implemented and validated ADC sampling, signal scaling, and calibration logic to ensure accurate voltage measurements
Wrote low-level peripheral drivers and configured registers for ADC, GPIO, SPI, and I2C operation from scratch
Integrated SPI and I2C peripherals to interface with external displays and analog-to-digital converters
Implemented data formatting and conversion logic to translate raw ADC readings into user-readable voltage output
Debugged noise, timing, and communication issues using oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, improving measurement stability and reliability

projects.title: MAGLEV Control System
projects.spec: PI + PID+FF cascade · QUARC hardware · ~1.5% overshoot
bullets: Modeled and analyzed a nonlinear magnetic levitation system, capturing both electrical and electro-mechanical dynamics
Derived system equations using first principles (Newton's laws & circuit laws) and linearized the model for control design
Designed a hierarchical control system with inner-loop PI current controller (fast response, ~1.5% overshoot, near-zero steady-state error) and outer-loop PID + feedforward ball position controller
Tuned controller parameters to meet performance specs including low overshoot, fast settling time, and zero steady-state error
Validated system performance by comparing Simulink simulations with real experimental results, identifying effects like sensor noise and system nonlinearities
Implemented real-time control using MATLAB/Simulink with QUARC, interfacing directly with the physical MAGLEV hardware
Analyzed trade-offs between response speed, damping, and accuracy during controller tuning

projects.title: Diet Optimization, Sugarscape Simulation
projects.spec: Stable optimum: ~40% protein · 39% carbs · 21% fats
bullets: Designed and implemented an agent-based Sugarscape simulation to study how macronutrient distributions (protein, carbohydrates, fats) impact long-term fat loss outcomes
Modeled human metabolism using Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR), caloric intake, caloric deficit, and body-fat dynamics grounded in established nutritional science
Implemented dynamic agent behavior where movement range, activity level, and survival depended on available energy from carbohydrates and fats within a regenerating nutrient environment
Developed a quantitative scoring metric based on proximity to a target body-fat percentage (15.5%) to evaluate diet effectiveness across thousands of simulation time steps
Identified a stable optimal macronutrient distribution of approximately 40% protein, 39% carbohydrates, and 21% fats; validated results against real-world nutritional guidelines
Produced data visualizations tracking population dynamics, nutrient distributions, and steady-state behavior
Built the simulation as a scalable framework extensible to gender-specific models, additional metabolic variables, and personalized diet optimization

projects.title: Enhanced System Monitoring, Glances
projects.spec: NVMe metrics · Full test coverage · UML architecture
bullets: Utilized UML to extract and document the architectural design of an open-source system monitoring tool, highlighting class structures and subsystem interactions
Addressed critical user feedback by developing features to improve data visibility and usability, including file system descriptions and optimized metric displays
Designed and implemented NVMe-specific metrics such as temperature, health status, and performance tracking to modernize hardware monitoring capabilities
Collaborated within a team using SCRUM methodology, managed sprints via JIRA, and utilized GitHub for version control
Developed and executed automated test suites, achieving comprehensive test coverage for newly introduced features
alts: Glances system monitor with NVMe and enhanced metrics
